dims: rod in tension: D = sqrt(4P / (pi sigma_t)), rounded up to a preferred size
d2 = 2.0 x D, the rod diameter (outer diameter of eye) [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
d3 = 1.5 x D, the rod diameter (pin head and collar diameter) [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
t = 1.25 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of single eye) [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
t1 = 0.75 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of each fork plate) [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
t2 = 0.5 x D, the rod diameter (thickness of pin head) [NPTEL IIT KGP M4L2 fig 4.2.3.1]
gap between eye and fork base
notes: Sized for 1.25 x the given load (62,500 N), then checked at 50,000 N. That margin is why the checks sit below their limits.
Pin raised to 45 mm for bending (needs 43.7 mm), the same step the NPTEL worked problem takes. Set pin_bending.mode to 'check_only' to keep the pin equal to the rod.
